name: MO-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district with a -21 point partisan lean
Incumbent Eric Burlison running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Democratic challenger Missi Hesketh has raised only about $50,000 with no outside support

model.rationale: This southwest Missouri seat sits about 21 points Republican-leaning, and incumbent Eric Burlison holds every practical advantage: a roughly 29-to-1 fundraising edge over Missi Hesketh, no outside spending against him, and no expert raters flagging the race as competitive. Markets price his win probability near 96%, consistent with a margin around 19 points Republican.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or a surge of outside spending against Burlison would be needed to put this district in play, and neither is evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Missouri's 7th District is a deeply Republican seat in the state's southwest corner, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Eric Burlison is running for reelection and faces Democrat Missi Hesketh and a Libertarian candidate in the general election.

Burlison has raised about $1.46 million and holds roughly $958,000 on hand, while Hesketh has raised about $51,000 with $34,000 available and no recorded outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets give Burlison about a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals point to a comfortable incumbent victory, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
